scope: Targeted primary-source basis for positive finite-time updates of a prescribed replenished monodisperse capture bath. Three sources; not a general integrator survey.
evidence_state: Published transient Markov and truncation methods, local analytic derivations and implemented sectional bath adaptations. Numerical controls are reported in collision_jump_results.md; no closed-aggregation solution or physical snow validation.
external_bytes: No full papers or external datasets added to the repository. Browser text extraction was inspected; source-byte hashes were not retained.

sources.authors: Donald Gross and Douglas R. Miller
sources.title: The Randomization Technique as a Modeling Tool and Solution Procedure for Transient Markov Processes
sources.reading_extent: Publisher metadata and abstract only. Full derivations, implementation comparisons and figures were not read.
sources.retrieval_limits: Publisher-indexed abstract retrieved; full article not obtained.
sources.evidence: Primary development of randomization for transient Markov probabilities and event statistics.
sources.use: Method lineage for the uniformized birth-ladder transition.
sources.limit: Abstract-level reading does not establish the detailed algorithm or performance of the local snow adaptation.

sources.authors: Bennett L. Fox and Peter W. Glynn
sources.title: Computing Poisson Probabilities
sources.reading_extent: Published six-page PDF text: abstract and §§1–4, including the weight algorithm, numerical stability, truncation selection and Poisson-tail bounds. Later probability-bound proofs and extensions were not substantively read; no figures inspected.
sources.retrieval_limits: Author-hosted PDF text retrieved successfully; no byte identity retained.
sources.evidence: Primary numerical method for stable Poisson weights with bounded truncated probability.
sources.use: Method lineage for stable finite-mixture evaluation and explicit probability-tail controls. The local implementation uses its own mode-centered recurrence and Chernoff bounds rather than claiming the complete published algorithm.
sources.limit: Its probability or bounded-reward bounds do not alone bound unbounded first or second mass moments; no snow-specific performance evidence.

sources.title: The finite state projection algorithm for the solution of the chemical master equation
sources.version_read: Author-posted text extraction identifies the published 2006 article and DOI. Exact equivalence to publisher bytes was not verified.
sources.reading_extent: Abstract; §I discussion of time leaping; selected §II mathematical passages, Theorem 2.2 and its probability-bound argument, finite-state interpretation; indexed §III algorithm opening. No full example or figure review.
sources.retrieval_limits: LANL PDF retrieval timed out and Colorado State PDF returned 403. Author-posted text was available; neither failed PDF was admitted as inspected bytes.
sources.evidence: Primary finite-state projection method and probability-error bounds.
sources.use: Explicit accounting for probability leaving a computational state set.
sources.limit: Probability certificates do not establish mass-moment accuracy or validate a nonlinear closed-aggregation adaptation.

local_derivations: For a point initial state, constant-rate forward Euler gives capture-count variance mu*(1-mu); its conditional realizability bound is independent of population weight.
For the unbounded constant-rate birth ladder and point initial state, backward Euler gives a geometric count with mean mu and variance mu*(1+mu).
Exact constant-rate finite-time capture gives a Poisson shift mixture, preserving number and increasing normalized mass variance by donor_mass^2*mu.
Before stopping at a finite-domain exit: M1_new=M1+N*d*mu and M2_new=M2+2*d*mu*M1+N*d^2*(mu^2+mu).
State-dependent bath rates define a bidiagonal birth generator on actual masses m0+k*d; uniformization is positive when its dominating-rate bound is valid.
Sectional reconstruction and numerical state/probability truncation remain independent approximation sources; closed aggregation adds donor depletion and population-dependent rates.
For omitted Poisson counts, factorial-moment identities shift the tail thresholds and bound omitted number, first mass moment and second mass moment separately.
A finite actual-mass birth ladder can be coupled to its dominating Poisson process up to the first artificial-cap hit; the Poisson probability of at least C events bounds that hit probability.

An absorbing physical upper boundary U and donor mass d bound stopped mass by U+d, allowing accumulated omitted probability to bound subsequent raw moments separately from reconstruction and quadrature.
method_status: Implemented in collision_jumps.py and collision_birth.py; numerical controls and approximation limits recorded separately in collision_jump_results.md. Prior solvers and saved products remain unchanged.
